title: rpg maker mv not starting, any help?

posts.author: DaveyDragon
posts.body:
the main issues i´m having with are with the steam version of rpgmaker mv. every time i try to launch it, the steam button goes "running" the splash screen appears and then nothing happens. i know its not crashing because the task manager shows that no tasks are started whenever i try to launch rpgmaker mv. i know its not that my computer cannot run it because i can load up in stars and time just fine
so far, i´ve tried re-installing, installing directly into the computer´s disk, verifying file integrity, launching it out of steam, rebooting, run as administrator, and no luck so far. theres no plugins as i haven´t even been able to download any plugins to begin with, and i´ve only been able to find is one thread that isn´t quite the same:
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/steam-edition-of-rpg-maker-mv-not-opening.147410/

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
Do you by chance have multiple monitors? I had an issue the other day where mine wouldn't open after a file integrity verification/reinstall either.
The splash screen would show but the editor wouldn't open, it had an icon on the taskbar that didn't have a window to peek on, and the task manager showed it without issue. Once I disconnected all but one of the monitors the editor opened and has been fine since then.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
I can think of two or three more possibilities.
First, you need to know that if the Steam download cache is damaged, both verify and install will pretend everything is OK while not working at all.
so please go into steam support/help, search for download cache and you'll find a configuration option called "clear download cache".
do that (it will repair the download cache) and then try verify again.
second, you might have the wrong drivers installed, especially for your display card.
The problem here is that the maker uses OpenGL, and OGL is competition to Microsofts DirectX.
As a result if your display driver is programmed by Microsoft, then it sometimes does not offer full OGL support.
You'll need to replace the build-in drivers from Windows with the manufacturer's original drivers by running their setup downloaded from their website (nVidia, AMD or Intel depending on your graphics chip)
Third, can you give us your computer specifications so we can check for compatibility?
especially important is the RAM and your exact display chip.
